mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech replacement engine typically costs £650-£1,500 for a used unit, £1,200-£2,400 for a reconditioned unit, or £2,000-£4,000 for a rebuilt unit with 12-month warranty. Supply & fit labour adds approximately £400-£800.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain tensioner failure in a Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, lasting 2-3 seconds. Other symptoms include rough idling, loss of power, and the engine management light illuminating. If left unaddressed, timing chain failure can cause catastrophic engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 508 1.6 PureTech worth £8,000-£18,000, replacement is often worthwhile if the rest of the car is in good condition. If the vehicle is worth under £8,000, a used engine or targeted repair may be more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech engines are dispatched within 24-48 hours, with supply & fit installation typically completed within 1-2 working days at approved garages.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech replacement engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rebuilt Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech engines include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically carry 3-6 months cover depending on supplier terms. Always verify warranty terms before purchase.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 1.6 PureTech and the 1.6 THP in the Peugeot 508?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.6 THP (EP6DT) was fitted to the first-generation 508 (2011-2018) and is known for timing chain tensioner issues. The 1.6 PureTech (EP6FDT) replaced it on the second-generation 508 (2018 onwards), offering improved reliability, better efficiency, and power outputs of 180hp or 225hp.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 1.6 PureTech arrived with the second-generation Peugeot 508 in 2018, replacing the earlier 1.6 THP with a more refined turbocharged petrol unit. Offered in 180hp and 225hp guises, it became the core petrol option for the Gen 2 508 range, delivering responsive performance with direct injection efficiency.

milestones.description: EP6FDT (1.6L, 180hp) launched with the Gen 2 508 liftback and SW estate
EP6FDT (1.6L, 225hp) introduced as the range-topping petrol option for GT and GT Line trims
EP6FDT receives minor calibration updates for Euro 6d emissions compliance
Facelift styling with minor updates; engine families unchanged
1.6 PureTech production ends with the Gen 2 508

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech is a responsive turbocharged petrol engine, but EP6FDT timing chain tensioner wear and high-pressure fuel pump failures dominate replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Use the problem groups below to compare repair costs versus replacement value for your specific 1.6 PureTech.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why EP6FDT 1.6 PureTech Engines Rattle on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The hydraulic timing chain tensioner can lose pressure, allowing chain slack. This causes a characteristic rattling noise on cold starts and, if left unaddressed, can lead to valve-to-piston contact on this interference-design engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner, guides, chain; reset ECU adaptation
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught before noise worsens; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Cylinder Head Inspection + Chain Kit
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove head to inspect valves; replace damaged components + full chain system
repairOptions.longevity: Appropriate if early valve contact suspected; adds cost uncertainty

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt EP6FDT with Upgraded Tensioner
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt EP6FDT unit with upgraded tensioner, dyno tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when valves damaged or engine has 80k+ miles; eliminates repeat risk

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech of 2018-2022 vintage is worth approximately £8,000-£18,000 depending on mileage and condition [INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]. For vehicles worth £8,000-£15,000, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components typically justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. For vehicles worth over £15,000, replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: On a Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech, preventative chain replacement at the first sign of cold-start rattle is cost-effective and prevents more serious engine damage. If rattling is present or a compression test shows valve damage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded tensioner is the safer long-term investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EP6FDT Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech engine prices

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - Why EP6FDT 1.6 PureTech Engines Lose Power
problems.rootCause: The high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) on EP6FDT direct-injection engines can suffer from internal wear, leading to low fuel rail pressure, misfires, and reduced power. The P0087 fault code is commonly associated with this issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove old HPFP; fit new/remanufactured unit; calibrate fuel system
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if engine otherwise healthy; may need in-tank pump check

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace HPFP; test and clean injectors; full fuel system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if injector leak-off is also detected

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt EP6FDT with Upgraded Fuel System
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with upgraded HPFP and fuel system components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when engine has 90k+ miles or shows additional wear

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech worth £8,000-£18,000, HPFP replacement is cost-effective if the engine is otherwise sound. For higher-mileage examples or vehicles with additional issues, a rebuilt EP6FDT unit offers better long-term value.
problems.recommendation: If your 1.6 PureTech shows the P0087 fault code or suffers from intermittent power loss, have the HPFP inspected immediately. If the vehicle has exceeded 90,000 miles or shows other wear signs, a rebuilt engine with upgraded fuel system components eliminates repeat risk.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EP6FDT Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech engine prices

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - Why Direct-Injection 1.6 PureTech Engines Lose Efficiency
problems.rootCause: Direct injection means fuel is sprayed directly into the combustion chamber, bypassing the intake valves. Over time, oil vapour and crankcase gases cause carbon deposits to accumulate on the intake valves, restricting airflow and reducing performance.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Walnut Blast Intake Valve Cleaning
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold; blast valves with walnut media; reassemble
repairOptions.longevity: Effective restoration of lost power and efficiency

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Walnut blast cleaning plus injector testing and ultrasonic cleaning
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if injector performance is also degraded

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt EP6FDT with Cleaned Intake System
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with decarbonised intake system, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when engine has 100k+ miles or shows additional wear

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Peugeot 508 1.6 PureTech, walnut blast cleaning every 60,000-80,000 miles is a worthwhile maintenance investment to maintain performance and fuel economy.
problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is an inevitable consequence of direct injection. A walnut blast cleaning at 60,000-80,000 miles is cost-effective and restores lost performance. If the vehicle has exceeded 100,000 miles or shows other issues, a rebuilt engine with a fully decarbonised intake system offers the best long-term solution.
